THE CORE IDEA

runs.text: Excludability asks whether nonpayers can be kept out; rivalry asks whether one person's use reduces another's. Public goods are nonexcludable and nonrival, common resources are nonexcludable and rival, club goods are excludable and nonrival, and private goods are excludable and rival. For efficient provision, marginal social benefit (MSB) equals marginal cost (MC).

WORKED EXAMPLE: VERTICAL SUMMATION

runs.text: Benefit / cost ($ thousands) is vertical; Community fireworks displays is horizontal. At four shared displays, North marginal benefit is $30 thousand and South marginal benefit $20 thousand. Their vertical sum, MSB $50 thousand, equals MC $50 thousand, making four displays efficient.

transcript.sourceText: At four community fireworks displays, North's marginal benefit is $30,000 and South's is $20,000. Because both communities consume the same shared quantity, MSB is the vertical sum: $50,000. MC is also $50,000, so four displays are efficient. Summing quantities horizontally would be incorrect.
